amendments: A1: recognizer analysis window limited to first 60 terms (performance of Berlekamp-Massey on large integers); made after a timing test of a single rule and before any complete run; the only orbit endpoints inspected were those of one rule during that test

recognizers.family_tests: subset: >=8 distinct terms all in family; consecutive: 8 successive terms are consecutive members in increasing order
recognizers.linear_recurrence: Berlekamp-Massey over Q, order<=4, n>=4r+6, verified on every term; min length V:22, R:10; analysis window = first 60 terms of each sequence (amendment A1)
sequences: V (vertex sequence; pre-periodic part if cyclic)

success_criterion: orbit status in {escape,horizon} AND (linrec_V or linrec_R present OR family consecutive hit on V or R). 'Fibonacci-like': family fibonacci consecutive on V or R, or linear recurrence a_n=a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}.

target_blindness.TB1: a selector is a rule tuple of the predeclared grammar; one interpreter; no per-sequence code
target_blindness.TB2: reads only X, H (window<=2), NB(X); class M additionally the visited set (unbounded memory; reference class, not finite control)
target_blindness.TB3: no step counter, target, index or external table; horizon and escape bound act outside the selector; recognizers have no feedback
target_blindness.TB4: the registered rule set, starts and horizon are the same for every sequence family and were fixed before the registered run; rules added after seeing results are labelled exploratory
target_blindness.TB5: audit: channel-read log, locality re-execution from (x,H) alone, brute-force cross-check of NB for small x
